digest.component_or_area: tickets branch push delivery (async, library, MCP surfaces)
propositions: A failed tickets push (rejected by remote pre-receive hook) never delivers its warning to three surfaces: async path spawns detached process with stderr=/dev/null, library embedders install NullHandler blocking stderr, and MCP agents read only tool result not server stderr.
The defect compounds with lock-contention-induced pending state (15s merge lock timeout against 48s+ compact lock hold), making push-pending state routine yet invisible on mute surfaces.

A durable marker recorded unconditionally at the single _raise_if_strict choke point (before conditional raise) makes failure observable despite detached stderr, missing handler, or MCP envelope—and clears on successful push.
MCP write-tool results widen from {result: str} to {result: str, push_status: {state, reason, detail, remote_ref, unpushed, since}} maintaining strict superset contract.
rebar.push_status() library call returns pending state regardless of whether stderr handler is installed, fixing in-process embedder surface.

Non-failure reasons (push-disabled, remote-not-found, invalid-destination, async-delivery-unobservable) exclude local-only stores from permanent pending alarm-fatigue; only terminal delivery failures record state.
